clue.text: He has the audacity to keep movin' slowly over English language

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the next
the first piece keeps, or holds, the second inside it

parts.note: a man who has the audacity is one who dares: MAN DARES
moving slowly is inching; the clipped g of movin' tells us to drop it too

explanation.surface: A cheeky fellow dawdles his way over to England, an image of nerve and slow progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts INCHIN inside MAN DARES, and 'over' sets E below them in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the principal spoken form of Chinese, a language in its own right.

clue.text: See 23
See 22
A metal in purplish element

indicators.note: the article and metal are placed in the colour word

parts.note: plum is a dark purplish colour
tin is a common metal

explanation.surface: Some metal sits within a purple-tinged chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a chemical element, number 78 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Second winter abroad, feel the cold?

parts.note: hiver is the French word for winter, so winter as said abroad

explanation.surface: Spending another winter overseas, does one feel chilly?
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling with chill is how a body reacts when it feels the cold, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Aggressive incursion's beginning, island inspired by vision

indicators.note: to be inspired, breathed in, by something is to go inside it

parts.note: a vision is a beautiful woman, a belle

indicators.note: the beginning of the word incursion's is its opening letter

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A military incursion starts with an aggressive plan to take an island, drawn up by a visionary.
explanation.walkthrough: A vision in the old sense is a stunningly beautiful woman, which the surface hides behind a seer's dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose is a straightforward synonym for warlike or hostile, eager to fight.

clue.text: Fiddle with just over three prawns

parts.note: a fiddle is a swindle or scam
pi is about 3.14, just over three

explanation.surface: Someone tampers with the portion, giving just over three prawns.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi is a dish of breaded prawns or langoustines, common in British pubs.

clue.text: Anxious to have those soldiers close to privates?

definitions.meaning: to have this phrase is to be restless and fidgety
ants are soldier insects, and privates (genitals) are inside trousers, so insects in the trousers

explanation.surface: Nervous about army soldiers getting close to the lowest-ranked troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Privates looks military, matching soldiers, but here means private parts; soldiers are soldier ants.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone so restless and agitated they cannot sit still, an image of jittery nerves.

clue.text: Possible words on meeting Scottish banker and a retired clerical leader

indicators.note: having retired, gone back, the string is read backwards

parts.note: hallo is something one might say on meeting someone
the Tay is a river in Scotland, and a river has banks

explanation.surface: A greeting on meeting a Scottish bank manager and a churchman who has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses HALLO TAY A in full.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shia Muslim cleric, especially in Iran.

clue.text: One's time is in the past

definitions.text: One's time is in the past

parts.words: One's time is in the past
parts.note: time here is a prison sentence, which this person has already served

explanation.walkthrough: Time is slang for a prison term, so the person whose time lies behind them is a former prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A former convict has finished doing time, so the sentence is over and behind them.

clue.text: Source of milk in powder going to China from Japan, say?

definitions.text: going to China from Japan, say?

indicators.note: the milk source is placed in the powder

parts.note: dust is a fine powder
a ewe gives sheep's milk

explanation.surface: Powdered milk being shipped from Japan to China.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies directly to the west of Japan, so travelling there means heading straight westward.

clue.text: See 26
Announcement of fitting ceremony

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: fitting means right or proper

explanation.surface: Someone announces a suitable ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a solemn ritual or ceremonial act, such as a religious observance.

clue.text: Violation among dissenting group — that's about right

parts.note: among means in

indicators.note: the first pieces go about, around, the next one

parts.note: a faction is a dissenting group within a party

explanation.surface: A breach of rules within a rebel faction, which someone claims is roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: An infraction is a breach of a rule or law, a synonym for a violation.

clue.text: Sweet as a nut?

definitions.meaning: a sweet is a dessert or cake, such as a rich fruit-filled one
a nut is a crazy person, which this word also means in slang

explanation.walkthrough: Sweet as a nut is a British idiom for perfectly fine, but the clue splits it into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a cake full of dried fruit and, in slang, an eccentric or mad person.

clue.text: Panacea for a silent guitarist?

definitions.meaning: a panacea is a supposed cure-all remedy
a guitarist who makes no sound has ...

explanation.surface: Seeking a remedy for a guitarist who will not play.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine or pet scheme claimed to fix everything, like a cure-all.

clue.text: Crush hand in trapping ring

parts.note: to hand something over is to pass it

indicators.note: the word in traps the ring letter inside it

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone crushes a hand when caught in a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A crush is an intense infatuation, a strong passionate feeling for someone.

clue.text: See 23
Unwelcome guest I book, more offensive

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
ruder means more offensive

explanation.surface: Someone books an even more objectionable visitor no one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder is someone who enters without permission, a guest nobody invited.

clue.text: Container secured by rushes, these causing extensive damage?

indicators.note: the container is secured, held, inside the rushes word

parts.note: rushes as a verb means hurries
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A container held in place by rushes amid destructive weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurricanes are violent tropical storms known for widespread destruction, an example of damage-causing forces.

clue.text: Half of roof gone, lift clear off

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word roof is its first two letters
in a down clue lifting the word raises it, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: clear, as in profit after deductions, is nett

explanation.surface: Half the roof is gone, so the lift has cleared off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' reverses NETT to TTEN in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is off has gone bad or decayed, the same as being spoiled.

clue.text: An educational officer in condor territory?

parts.note: a dean is a senior officer of a college or university

explanation.surface: An academic official goes searching for condors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean condor lives in the Andes mountains, so its territory is Andean by location.

clue.text: One bound to impress seller, if all goes well

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals

indicators.note: to impress is to press in, so the seller is pressed into the bound word

parts.note: bound means tied
a shop is a seller of goods

explanation.surface: Someone tied up in their work hopes to impress a seller, if things go well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to impress' is read literally as press in, so the bound word takes the seller inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses a hope about the outcome, much like saying if all goes well or fingers crossed.

clue.text: A heating unit a joke, apes surely miserable while inside

parts.note: a therm is a unit of heat used for gas billing
a jest is a joke

indicators.note: miserable suggests the letters are in a wretched, disordered state

explanation.surface: An absurd scene of a heater, a gag, and gloomy apes, all while locked indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserable' rearranges APES SURELY into YS PLEASURE. Inside means in prison here.
explanation.definitionFit: British courts detain prisoners for an indefinite term with this phrase, so it means locked up in jail.

clue.text: Recorded, month one, century back

indicators.note: back means the whole string reads backwards

parts.note: Dec is short for December, a month
one is I in Roman numerals
a ton is a hundred, a century in cricket

explanation.surface: Something was recorded one month, a century ago.
explanation.definitionFit: To have noticed something is to have observed and registered it, much like recorded.

clue.text: China from Japan, an inevitability while going 11

indicators.note: the answer to 11 is due west; going west in an across clue means reading right to left

parts.note: a must is something that cannot be avoided
as can mean while

explanation.surface: Porcelain from Japan travels west to China, as it must.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going 11' reverses AMUSTAS. Satsuma is also a citrus fruit, but here it is the Japanese pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Satsuma ware is a type of Japanese pottery, and china is a general word for porcelain.

clue.text: Say it all — as might an audiobook reader?

definitions.meaning: to say it all is to be very revealing or expressive
an audiobook reader voices whole books aloud

explanation.walkthrough: Volumes literally means books, which an audiobook narrator voices one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to convey a great deal without words, like saying everything at once.

clue.text: Understanding a language for the most part, staff ending in conflict

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: Greek is a language
staff are employees, men

indicators.note: the ending of the word conflict is its last letter

explanation.surface: Mutual understanding in a shared language, mostly, while staff end up in conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the K from GREEK.
explanation.definitionFit: An understanding between parties is a deal or accord, a synonym for agreement.
